note: Pragmatics gold for the cross-domain case: the authoritative SOURCE OF TRUTH (realm) for each shared requirement field at the seam. X = Meridian (transport), Y = Cascade (IP), shared = a co-owned demarcation. Semantic correspondence is necessary but not sufficient; provisioning across the seam also requires respecting whose realm owns each field's value, and the characteristic pragmatic error is letting the wrong realm govern (a requirer claiming a value the other realm realises, or transport claiming everything it carries).

fields.why: the realised one-way latency is a physical property of the transport path; the IP side states only a tier requirement
protection is realised by the transport path (the diverse route); the IP side requires it but does not own its realisation
the class of service is scheduling in the IP routers, owned by the IP realm; the transport 'grade' is an unrelated transport class and must not claim authority here
the committed information rate is the customer's IP-service SLA commitment; transport must carry it, but the authoritative committed value is the IP side's, not the bearer line rate
the hand-off and the attachment are one co-owned demarcation; neither side's local naming overrides the other, they must agree it is the same point
